# chiplog

> One wide log event per operation for Node, instead of scattered lines you have to reassemble.
> Also known as canonical log lines (Stripe) or wide events.

chiplog accumulates named stages through a whole operation — at any depth, via AsyncLocalStorage,
with nothing threaded through call signatures — and flushes a single record when the operation
settles. Zero dependencies; the sink is supplied by the caller, so it never competes with the
logger already in the project.

Key properties:
- `run(label, fn)` is a wrapper, not a start/end pair: an exception is attributed to the stage that
  was running and rethrown unchanged, so a flow that threw cannot report `ok`.
- Everything entering an event is bounded (stages, depth, width, string length) and passed through a
  redaction hook, so one pathological flow cannot break the log pipeline or leak PII.
- W3C `traceparent` is the carrier across services and queues; no bespoke format.
- Reserved-key collisions from `set()` are reported in `shadowedFields`, never silently dropped.

## Docs

- [Quick start](https://chiplog.dev/docs/quick-start/): install, sink, first flow
- [Stages and fields](https://chiplog.dev/docs/stages/): ambient recording, naming, `set()`
- [Failures](https://chiplog.dev/docs/failures/): attribution, non-Error throws, `fail()`
- [Correlation](https://chiplog.dev/docs/correlation/): traceparent, queues, nested flows
- [Redaction and limits](https://chiplog.dev/docs/safety/): PII hook, bounds, hostile values
- [Adapters](https://chiplog.dev/docs/adapters/): Hono, Elysia, writing your own
- [API reference](https://chiplog.dev/docs/api/): every export and option
